Use local sub-agents only for bounded independent work. Do not rely on remote agent-to-agent delegation or hidden state as provenance. jobs.title: Design RFC 0036 MCP harness from Codex
jobs.objective: Produce an implementation design for RFC 0036: the agent-facing harness for the daemon V2 mutation surface. Cover (a) the new `striatum-mcp` skill: claude_code + generic template bodies, fan-out wiring through `CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS`, generic concatenation, gemini-guide append, plugin-bundle regeneration; (b) the two new closed-set chat tools `generate_workflow_preview` + `generate_workflow_write` extending RFC 0023 V1.5: tool input schemas, dispatch glue to the RFC 0034 V1 service endpoints, operator-confirmation gate reuse from RFC 0013 step 7, mutation-not-allowed path handling. State the threat surfaces explicitly: prompt-injected MCP client requesting elevated mutation, capability token leaked across repos, operator-confirmation bypass attempt, audit-chain coverage for both tools, denial-vocabulary handling.

jobs.title: Design RFC 0036 MCP harness from Claude Code
jobs.objective: Produce an implementation design for RFC 0036 emphasizing trust boundaries (operator, daemon, MCP client, chat session) and operator-mistake footguns: short-lived token issuance posture, capability scope semantics (repo_id-scoped vs daemon-global), default-deny enforcement when an MCP method requires a capability the token lacks, audit row append for every mutating chat-tool call including denials, operator-confirmation gesture that the chat model cannot bypass, mutation-not-allowed path that hides write tools from `tools/list` rather than emitting confusing errors. Address how a prompt-injected chat model that tries to escalate via false identity claims is contained by capability-token authority.

jobs.title: Design RFC 0036 MCP harness from Gemini
jobs.objective: Produce an implementation design for RFC 0036 covering cross-platform reality of the MCP harness: skill body discoverability across claude_code / codex / gemini profiles, plugin regeneration semantics across `.claude-plugin/` / `.codex-plugin/` / `gemini-extension.json`, chat tool dispatch wiring against the existing RFC 0023 V1.5 closed-set framework, and adversarial test cases: hostile chat client requesting `tools/list` to enumerate tools, expired token replay attempt, revoked token replay attempt, scope-mismatch (token scoped to repo A trying to write into repo B through the chat tool), operator-confirmation bypass attempt, audit chain tamper attempt via the chat path. State which parts are cross-platform and which need platform-specific work.

jobs.title: Synthesize RFC 0036 MCP harness implementation plan
jobs.objective: Reconcile all three fresh design artifacts into one implementation plan for RFC 0036. Pick the concrete `striatum-mcp` skill body shape (what sections, in what order, with what example invocations), the chat tool input/output schemas, the dispatch wiring against the existing RFC 0023 V1.5 closed-set framework, the operator-confirmation gate reuse path, the mutation-not-allowed path semantics, the plugin-regeneration story, and the test coverage strategy. Explicitly defer the `examples/` workflow that exercises the chat-generate flow end-to-end (it can land in a follow-up). State the staging plan: skill body first, then chat tool wiring, then mutation-not-allowed path, then docs, then plugin regeneration.

jobs.title: Threat-model review of RFC 0036 design
jobs.objective: Review the synthesized MCP harness plan under threat_model posture. Verdict acceptance means the design enumerates the trust boundaries the MCP harness introduces and each is acknowledged or mitigated. Scope per RFC 0031 §Threat Model: defend against over-eager AI agents acting through documented interfaces and operator-mistake footguns; malicious-local-root is OUT OF SCOPE. Check: capability gating on every chat tool route; operator-confirmation gate that the chat model cannot bypass; audit row appended for every mutating chat-tool call including denials; mutation-not-allowed path hides write tools from `tools/list` rather than emitting partial-information errors; default-deny enforcement when a tool requires a capability the token lacks; no global mutation flag bypass; no chat-model-claimed-identity escalation; capability scope mismatch (token scoped to repo A used against repo B through the chat tool) refused with documented denial vocabulary. Reviewers should flag any text resembling 'trusted chat client' framing as overclaim. IMPORTANT: when writing the review artifact, write the file directly. Do not surface strategy and ask the operator to proceed; the dogfood-036 gemini friction pattern is documented in `docs/dogfood/036/OPERATOR_REPORT.md` intervention #2 — do not repeat it. Produce the artifact at `docs/dogfood/038/review/design/threat/REVIEW.md` with valid striatum.finding.v1 front matter and the explicit verdict line.

jobs.title: Implement RFC 0036 MCP harness V1 slice
jobs.objective: Implement only the reviewed and accepted V1 slice from docs/dogfood/038/DESIGN_SYNTHESIS.md. Ship: `striatum-mcp` skill body (claude_code + generic templates) wired into `CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS`; chat tools `generate_workflow_preview` + `generate_workflow_write` extending the RFC 0023 V1.5 closed-set framework; dispatch wiring to the existing RFC 0034 V1 service endpoints; operator-confirmation gate reuse from RFC 0013 step 7; mutation-not-allowed path that hides write tools from `tools/list`; plugin bundle regeneration covering the new skill; documentation updates to SPEC, MCP, UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE, HOW_TO_AGENT, HOW_TO_HUMAN, RFC 0034 status (§10 deferral → implemented in RFC 0036), CHANGELOG, README. Use sub-agents aggressively for parallelizable work per the implement prompt. Cycle exhaustion at max_iterations=2 → operator records a decision artifact and continues with the latest verdict; do not block the run.

jobs.title: Threat-model review of RFC 0036 V1 build
jobs.objective: Review the implementation under threat_model posture: capability authorization correctness on every chat tool route, audit row appended for every mutating chat-tool call including denials, default-deny enforcement when a tool requires a capability the token lacks, mutation-not-allowed path correctness (write tools hidden from `tools/list` rather than emitting partial-information errors), operator-confirmation gate that the chat model cannot bypass, no chat-model-claimed-identity escalation, capability scope mismatch refused with documented denial vocabulary, audit chain integrity across the chat path, skill body teaches the correct denial-vocabulary recovery and capability scope semantics. The skill body must NOT contain text resembling 'trusted client' framing or wildcard-capability-grant guidance.
